lawyer:
Md Fazlul Karim, Sheikh Shamsul Alam and Md Reza-e-Murshed Kamal, Advocates -For the Appellant. 
MA Samad, Advocate -For the Respondent
parties:
Yusuf Sarder (Md) Waqf Estate represented by the Mutawalli Md Tabarak Ali Sarder ------ Appellant
vs.
Md Hussain Khan ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Bijan Kumar Das, J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 7-9-1987 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 under section 35(3) of the Wakfs Ordinance setting aside those dated 21-2-1986 passed by the Waqf Administrator in Enrolment Case No. 1579 directing the Waqf Administrator to dispose of the said EC No. 15719 after the disposal of Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 pending in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. One Alhaj Md Hossain Khan filed an application under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 being Diary No. 5184 dated 17-10-1984 praying for cancellation of the enrolment made in the said EC No. 15719 in respect of Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder Waqf Estate on the allegation that the petitioner and another filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the schedule properties including other properties against the aforesaid Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder (now deceased) who was the sole defendant in the said suit. It is alleged that during tendency of the suit the defendant Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder created waqf of the suit property by a declaration dated 1-7-1976 and constituted himself as the first mutwalli of Yusuf Sarder Waqf Estate. It is stated in the application for cancellation of the enrolment that the property mentioned therein appertaining to Mouza Dhanmondi, Khatian No. 26 and plot Nos. 692-694 and 696 measuring 0.24 katha 2 chhatak belonged to the petitioner and his co-sharers and their uncle Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder had no interest in the said property but he fraudulently created a waqf in respect of the said property and got it enrolled in EC No. 15719. It is stated that no notice for enrolment of the suit property as waqf property was served on the co-sharers and they prayed for cancellation of the enrolment of the property as waqf property.

2. The Administrator of Waqf heard the matter and by order dated 21-2-1986 rejected the prayer for cancellation on the finding that there was no reasonable ground to declare the property as secular property.

<u>3. Being aggrieved thereby the said Md Hossain Khan submitted a petition under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 to the learned District Judge and that the learned District Judge by the impugned judgment and order noticed that Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 for declaration of title and recovery of possession was filed by the said Md Hossain Khan against the Wakif Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder (since deceased) and during pendency of the suit the said wakif Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder created the wakf-e-Lillah on 1-7-1976 and accordingly, the transfer in question was hit under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act. The learned District Judge further found that the present mutwalli Md Tobarak Ali Sikder had instituted Title Suit No. 247 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge against the petitioner Md Hossain Khan for a decree for declaration that the suit land was waqf property but subsequently, the said suit was dismissed for want of tadbir. The learned District Judge further noticed that on the basis of a direction of the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 200 of 1979 the Administrator enrolled the property as waqf property and the Administration of Waqfs while deciding the application filed under section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance considered irrelevant issues but did not consider the relevant issue as to whether the wakif had title in the property in question and the property was made waqf in accordance with law. In any view, the learned District Judge noticed that the Administrator of Waqf should decide the application filed under section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance after the disposal of Title Suit No. 27 of 1974. Accordingly, by order dated 7-9-1987 the learned District Judge set aside the judgment and order of the Waqf Administrator dated 21-2-1986 in connection with EC No. 15719 and directed that the matter may be re-heard and disposed of after disposal of Title Suit No. 27 of 1974.</u>

4. Being aggrieved thereby Alhaj Md Tobarak Ali Sikder being the mutawali of the alleged Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder Waqf Estate preferred the Miscellaneous Appeal before this court.

5. Mr Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Senior Advocate on behalf of the appellant, has taken me through the judgments of the courts below including the judgment of the Waqf Administrator and submits that under section 50 of Waqfs Ordinance only the Administrator of Waqfs may decide if the property in question is waqf property or not and the civil Court is excluded from deciding the said question. The learned Senior Advocate further submits that section 102 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 is a bar in entertaining any suit inasmuch as it is provided therein that except as otherwise expressly provided in the said Ordinance, no decision or order of the Administrator shall be questioned in any suit or other proceeding in any court. In support of his submission the learned Advocate for the appellant relied on a decision in the case of Syed Shah Mohammad Osman Ghani vs Bangladesh, through Secy. Ministry of Public Works and Urban Dev and others reported in 39 DLR 451 and in the case of Syed Masud Ali and others vs Md Asmatullah and others reported in 32 DLR (AD) 39. Mr Karim also relied on a decision in the case of Afazuddin Mollah and others vs Mobarak Ali Munshi and others reported in 46 DLR 587.

6. Mr MA Samad, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent, submits that the present respondent along with two others instituted Title Suit No. 57 of 1973 against the Wakif Alhaj Yusuf Sarder praying for declaration of title and recovery of possession. The said suit was transferred several times and it was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 27 of 1974, Title Suit No. 333 of 1992, thereafter Title Suit No. 1 of 1994 of the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and the alleged wakif created the alleged waqf property during pendency of the said suit on 1-7-1976 and thus the alleged transfer shall be subject to the decision to be passed in the Civil Suit. According to Mr MA Samad, the aforesaid Title Suit No. 57 of 1973 which was ultimately re-numbered as Title Suit No. 1 of 1994 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka was decreed in favour of the plaintiffs and the said decree was set aside by the appellate Court but in revision the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court whereupon a Civil Petition for leave to appeal was filed before the Appellate Division which was subsequently dismissed. A review application was then filed before the Appellate Division but the review was also dismissed. Mr Samad therefore submits that the civil Court has decided the question that the property dedicated by the wakif Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder as wakf-e-Lillah was a secular property belonging to the plaintiffs of the suit and also directed recovery of possession of the suit property and accordingly, the property in question could not be treated as waqf property. Mr Samad therefore, submits that the impugned decision of the learned District Judge passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 under section 35(3) of the Waqfs Ordinance is required to be modified inasmuch as civil Court has decided the Title Suit and it is no more necessary to re-hear the cancellation matter by the Waqf Administrator in connection with EC No. 15719 any more and this court may decide the matter finally.

7. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the impugned orders and all other connected papers. It appears from the judgment of the learned District Judge and also from the order of the Waqf Administrator in EC No. 15719 that Title Suit No. 57 of 1973 was instituted by Md Hossain Khan and two others against the alleged wakif Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder and that during pendency of the said suit the aforesaid Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder created the waqf on 1-7-1976 in respect of the property in question. From additional paper book filed by the appellant it appears that Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder filed a written statement in the said Title Suit No. 57 of 1973 on 21-12-1973 but did not claim the waqf nature of the property in question. In the written statement the wakif Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder did not claim that he had created wakf-e-Lillah in respect of the property involved in the suit. There is therefor no hesitation in holding that the alleged waqf was created on 1-7-1976 during pendency of Title Suit No. 57 of 1973. Thus the Administrator of Waqfs illegally enrolled the property as wakif-e-Lillah on 21-2-1986 on the basis of an order passed by the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 200 of 1979. In that view of the matter, when waqf property was created during of a civil suit in a competent civil Court for declaration of title, the waqf administrator was not permitted to invoke adjudicatory jurisdiction under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance. In the present case also the wakf administrator had no jurisdiction to enroll the property as waqf property as wakif-e-Lillah on 21-2-1986 as the civil suit being Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 was not decided till then and the waqf administrator committed a gross error of law in allowing enrolment of the property in question as waqf-e-Lillah at a time when the suit for declaration of title in a competent civil Court was pending.

8. Mr MA Samad, the learned Advocate for the respondent, has submitted an additional affidavit enclosing certified copy of the judgments passed in the civil suit by the trial Court, by the lower appellate Court, by the High Court Division and by the Appellate Division. It is stated that Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 was ultimately re-numbered as Title Suit No. 1 of 1994 of the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka and the trial Court by judgment and decree dated 26-6-1995 decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff Md Hossain Khan and others declaring plaintiffs 16 annas title in the suit land and directing recovery of possession. It is also stated that in the said suit that the present appellant claiming himself to be Mutawalli impleaded himself as defendant No. 28 and contested the suit and the aforesaid decree was passed on contest against defendant No. 28 and ex parte against the rest. The defendant No. 28 then preferred Title Appeal No. 194 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka and the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka by judgment and decree dated 20-4-1996 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree dated 26-5-1995 and 5-7-1995 respectively of the, trial Court. The present respondent then moved the High Court Division and obtained a Rule in Civil Revision No. 1495 of 1996. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 17-11-1994 made the Rule absolute set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court. Against the said decision of the High Court Division the present appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 194 of 2000 before the Appellate Division and their Lordship dismissed the said Leave Petition on 21-11-2001 maintaining the order of the High Court Division who restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court which decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff declaring plaintiffs sixteen annas title to the suit land and directing recovery of possession of the suit property. It is further stated that the present appellant then filed a Review. Petition No. 1 of 2002 before the Appellate Division for review of the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 194 of 2000 and their Lordship of the Appellate Division dismissed the said review petition on 26-10-2002. The certified copy of the judgments passed in the aforesaid matters have been enclosed with the additional affidavit filed by the respondent and marked Annexure A, B, C, D respectively. It thus appears that Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 which was finally re-numbered as Title Suit No. 1 of 1994 instituted by the present respondent and others against the wakif Alhaj Yusuf Sarder, who died during pendency of the suit was decreed declaring plaintiffs (present respondent) title to the suit property which was maintained up to the Appellate Division. Since the alleged waqf was created on 1-7-1976 during pendency of the title suit it cannot have any legal effect. The civil Court having decided the title in favour of the present respondent. Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder had no title in the property to create the alleged waqf on 1-7-1976. The transfer of the property as waqf property during pendency of the suit is hit by the doctrine of listeners under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act and the creation of the alleged waqf on 1-7-1976 is subject to the decision in Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 which was ultimately decided in favour of the present respondent, who was the plaintiff in the said suit and against Alhaj Md Yusuf Sarder (since deceased) who was the sole defendant in the said suit. The issue with respect to the nature and character of the property has been set at rest by the civil Court in a suit instituted before the creation of the alleged waqf declaring plaintiffs title and granting recovery of possession and thus the secular property could not be treated as waqf property. In the facts of the case the alleged wakf had no title in the property to create the waqf. After the decision of the civil Court in respect of the nature and character of the property in a suit instituted before the creation of the alleged Waqf the Waqf Administrator cannot invoke its adjudicatory jurisdiction to decide whether the property is waqf property or not as provided under section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance.

<u>9. The decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant in 39 DLR 451 has no application in the facts of the present case. in the said decision a Division Bench held—"The sole question of law raised is as to whether a plaintiff has the option to file a civil suit for a declaration that a particular property is waqf property although section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 provides that any question whether a particular property is waqf property or not shall be decided by the Administrator of Waqfs. The plaintiff-petitioner filed such a suit and also obtained an ex-parte decree. On appeal, the suit was dismissed on the sole ground that the suit was not maintainable in view of the provisions of section 50 of the said Ordinance." In the said decision their Lordships further held "Under section 102 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 no decision or order of the Administrator shall be questioned in any suit or other proceeding in any Court, except as otherwise expressly provided in the said Ordinance. The express ouster is attracted only after the Administrator has given a decision or order. In the entire Ordinance we do not find any express ouster forbidding the civil Courts to entertain any suit as to the waqf character of a suit property. It is only when the Administrator of Waqfs gives a decision or order in relation to the same that the bar of section 102 is attracted." In the present case the civil suit was instituted long before the creation of waqf and that the wakf in his written statement submitted in the said suit did not claim that he has created waqf in respect of the property in question. The waqf administrator allowed enrolment of the property on the basis of an order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 200 of 1979 by the learned District Judge, Dhaka though there is no such provision in the Waqfs Ordinance empowering the District Judge to pass an order for enrolment of a property as waqf property. Chapter 4 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 relates to enrolment of waqfs. Section 47 of the Waqfs Ordinance provides for enrolment of waqf and section 48 of the Waqfs Ordinance provides for register of waqfs. Section 49 of the Waqfs Ordinance provides power of the Administrator to cause enrolment of waqf and to amend the register and section 50 of Waqfs Ordinance provides that any question whether a particular property is waqf property or not shall be decided by the Administrator provided that the mutawalli or any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Administrator in this behalf may, within three months from the date of such decision or order, submit a petition to the District Judge in accordance with the provision of sub-section (1) of section 35; and if such a petition is filed, the provisions of section 35 shall apply. In the present case an application for cancellation of the enrolment was filed before the Administrator of waqfs under section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance on the ground that the property is not waqf property which was dismissed by the waqf administrator and the present respondent being aggrieved thereby filed a petition to the learned District Judge in accordance with sub-section 1 of section 35 and the learned District Judge passed the impugned order. The petition under section 35(1) of the Waqfs Ordinance filed before the learned District Judge empowers the learned District Judge to declare that the property is not a waqf property or that the property is waqf property within the limit stated in the petition. In view of my above finding that the property could not be a waqf property as decided in the civil suit and affirmed up to the Appellate Division it may be declared that the suit property is not a waqf property. The decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant, namely, 46 DLR 587 again has no manner of application in the facts of the present case. In the said decision a learned Single Judge considered sections 64(2), 35(3), 38 and 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance. I have already held that the waqf administrator, in the facts of the case, had no adjudicatory jurisdiction to invoke section 50 of the Waqfs Ordinance for the purpose of deciding whether the property in question is waqf property or not as the civil Court had decided the issue and has decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff declaring plaintiffs sixteen annas title and directing recovery of possession of the suit property. The decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant reported in 32 DLR (AD) 39 again has no manner of application in the facts of the present case. In view of my above findings I do not find any substance in this appeal.</u>

10. In the result this appeal is dismissed with modification that the property in question is not waqf property and the Waqf Administrator is not required to decide the question as directed by the learned District Judge in the impugned Order dated 7-9-1987 in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986.

In the facts of the case, I do not make any order as to costs.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
